newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-EUROPEAN CUP IN DOUBT AFTER BROADCASTERS PULL OUT.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-EUROPEAN CUP IN DOUBT AFTER BROADCASTERS PULL OUT.

text.p: Organisers of this season's European Cup club tournament insisted on Tuesday the competition would start as scheduled next month despite the decision by British host broadcasters ITV to withdraw their interest.

The expanded tournament, involving clubs and provinces from all Europe's major rugby-playing nations, is due to start on October 12 with the opening round-robin matches in England, Wales, Ireland and France.
The entire timetable, with the final scheduled for January 4, must now be in doubt but tournament director Roger Pickering said discussions had already started with other broadcasters.

"The European Cup is too important a tournament not to be televised and it is our responsibility to try and achieve the widest possible audience for what will be an outstanding competition," Pickering said.
An ITV spokesperson said: "Over the past few weeks, we have been discussing terms under which ITV could take up its option for future coverage of the European Rugby Cup.
"Unfortunately, and despite goodwill on both sides, we were unable to reach a mutually-acceptable agreement with European Rugby Cup Ltd."
